title: Cybersecurity capstone: design a safer organization
subtitle: Create a measured plan combining risk, controls, owners, response exercises and review.
description: Create a measured plan combining risk, controls, owners, response exercises and review. Guided explanations, six original visual diagrams, safe practice, trusted resource links, worked examples and a randomized quiz.

blocks.text: Lesson 10 — Cybersecurity capstone: design a safer organization

LEARNING OUTCOME
Create a measured plan combining risk, controls, owners, response exercises and review.

Safety rule: work only with devices, accounts and training applications you own or have explicit written permission to assess. Use synthetic information. A public system or a suspicious person is not permission.

Use a fictional organization. Identify its important data and services, list risks, select a few controls, assign owners and define how success will be measured. Use NIST CSF to organize outcomes rather than treating a framework as a list of products.

blocks.caption: Visual 1/6 — Governance. Use it to explain how the controls or workflow connect.
Visual 2/6 — Protect controls. Use it to explain how the controls or workflow connect.

blocks.text: Examples include account MFA coverage, critical patch compliance, restore-test success, alert acknowledgement time, and closure rate for validated findings. State a baseline, target, data source, owner and review cadence. Metrics should support decisions, not reward misleading numbers.

blocks.caption: Visual 3/6 — Detect signals. Use it to explain how the controls or workflow connect.
Visual 4/6 — Response plan. Use it to explain how the controls or workflow connect.

blocks.text: Run a tabletop for a lost device, compromised administrator session or service outage. Keep it simulated, notify participants and avoid real customer data. Record decisions, identify missing contacts, update the response plan and schedule a follow-up review.

blocks.caption: Visual 5/6 — Recovery target. Use it to explain how the controls or workflow connect.
Visual 6/6 — Measure progress. Use it to explain how the controls or workflow connect.

blocks.text: Practice checklist: (1) read the lab rules, (2) use fabricated data or an isolated training target, (3) predict what the control should do, (4) test one small condition, (5) save only minimal evidence, and (6) explain the defensive follow-up. Stop and ask the owner if any target or action is outside the approved scope.

blocks.output: A measurable safeguard includes a baseline, target, owner and review date.

blocks.question: What makes a security metric useful?
options: A baseline, target, data source, owner and review schedule
A chart with no accountable owner
A slogan that cannot be measured
blocks.explanation: Measurable controls support decisions and continuous improvement.
blocks.hint: Use the lesson definitions and authorization boundary to reason through the options.

blocks.question: What should a tabletop exercise use?
options: A simulated scenario and agreed participants
blocks.explanation: A tabletop rehearses decisions without exposing real systems or data.
blocks.hint: Use the lesson definitions and authorization boundary to reason through the options.

blocks.question: Which approach better protects private information?
options: Use synthetic data and collect only necessary, authorized evidence
Copy all customer records for convenience
blocks.explanation: Data minimization and redaction reduce privacy and exposure risks.
blocks.hint: Use the lesson definitions and authorization boundary to reason through the options.

blocks.question: What is a sound step after applying a fix?
options: Retest the same authorized condition and document the result
blocks.explanation: Retesting verifies the correction and preserves a useful record.
blocks.hint: Use the lesson definitions and authorization boundary to reason through the options.

blocks.question: What should happen when a target is outside scope?
options: Stop and ask the owner to clarify permission
blocks.explanation: Scope is a boundary; do not proceed without permission.
blocks.hint: Use the lesson definitions and authorization boundary to reason through the options.
